title: Geometrically integral fibres descend to a tail of a directed ring system
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(A_j)_{j\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative rings with compatible unital transition maps, and let $A=\varinjlim_{j\in I}A_j$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $a\in I$ and a finitely presented $A_a$-algebra $C_a$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $C_j=C_a\otimes_{A_a}A_j$ for $j\geq a$ and $C=C_a\otimes_{A_a}A$ [def-weil-module-base-change] [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Suppose that for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ the fibre ring $C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is geometrically integral over the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there is $b\geq a$ such that for every $j\geq b$ and every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A_j$, the fibre ring $C_j\otimes_{A_j}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is geometrically integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Geometrically integral here means that its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is nonempty, reduced and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme] after every extension of the residue field. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis, and no injectivity of a transition or colimit map, is assumed.

source.place: Tags 05FG (lemma-Noetherian-approximation-geometrically-reduced) and 05FH (lemma-Noetherian-approximation-geometrically-irreducible), proofs: simultaneous constructible-locus refinement of a fixed finite-presentation model, for an arbitrary directed base-ring system.

proof.text: Put $S_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$, and let $f_a:X_a\to S_a$ be the structure map. The spectrum-colimit lemma exhibits $S$ as the inverse limit of the $S_j$, with affine transitions; all $S_j$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the affine-scheme lemma. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $X_a\times_{S_a}S_j$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_j$ for $j\geq a$, and $X_a\times_{S_a}S$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$. The projections are the maps induced by the specified tensor-product structure maps.

For the given finitely presented map $A_a\to C_a$, let $E_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $E_{\mathrm{irr}}$ be the loci in $S_a$ supplied by the reduced-fibre-locus and irreducible-fibre-locus nodes. Both are constructible without flatness or Noetherian hypotheses. Their intersection $E=E_{\mathrm{red}}\cap E_{\mathrm{irr}}$ is constructible by the Boolean-algebra clause of the constructible-subset definition. By the definitions of geometric integrality and of an integral scheme, $E$ is exactly the locus where the fibre is geometrically integral: after every field extension it is reduced, irreducible and nonempty.

The component count used below detects geometric irreducibility. For a fibre $Z$ over a field $k$, choose the fixed separable closure $k_s$ and put $W=Z\times_k k_s$. If $Z$ is geometrically irreducible, $W$ is irreducible and nonempty, so its only maximal irreducible subset is $W$ itself. Conversely, if $W$ has exactly one irreducible component $D$, the component-covering lemma gives $W=D$; thus $W$ is irreducible and nonempty. Apply the subset-geometric-irreducibility lemma to the whole subset $|Z|$ and the separably closed extension $k_s/k$ to conclude irreducibility and nonemptiness after every field extension. Thus geometric irreducibility of a fibre is equivalent to its geometric component count being $1$; the empty fibre has count $0$.

source.place: Tag 055B (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-constructible), level n=1; topology.tex Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible); varieties.tex Tag 054P (lemma-geometrically-irreducible-check-after-extension).

proof.text: For any ring map $u:A_a\to B$, write $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to S_a$ and base change $f_a$ along $h$. At $q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ the fibre is the scalar extension of the fibre at $p=h(q)$: the affine fibre-product formula gives $(C_a\otimes_{A_a}B)\otimes_B\kappa(q)\cong C_a\otimes_{A_a}\kappa(q)$. Explicitly $(c\otimes b)\otimes\lambda\mapsto c\otimes\bar b\lambda$ has inverse $c\otimes\lambda\mapsto(c\otimes1)\otimes\lambda$; the tensor universal property verifies these maps on pure tensors. The reduced-fibre-locus node states equality of the reduced loci under this arbitrary base change. The geometric-component-count base-change node states equality of component counts at $q$ and $p$; step 3 identifies count $1$ with geometric irreducibility on each side. Intersecting these two equivalences shows that the geometrically integral fibre locus of this base change is exactly $h^{-1}(E)$. Neither implication requires $u$ to be injective or flat.

Apply step 4 to $A_a\to A$. The hypothesis says that its geometrically integral fibre locus is all of $S$, so the limit projection $S\to S_a$ has image contained in $E$. Apply the limit-contained-in-constructible lemma at the original index $a$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 (directed inverse system, quasi-compact quasi-separated stages, affine transitions, and the specified scheme limit) and step 2 (constructibility of $E$). It gives $b\geq a$ such that the image of $S_j\to S_a$ lies in $E$ for every $j\geq b$.

source.place: Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible), as used in the proofs of more-morphisms.tex Tags 05FG and 05FH.

proof.text: For every $j\geq b$, apply step 4 to $A_a\to A_j$. Since the image of $S_j\to S_a$ lies in $E$, every $q\in S_j$ has geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible fibre. After each extension of $\kappa(q)$ this fibre is reduced and irreducible, with nonemptiness supplied by irreducibility; it is therefore integral by the integral-scheme definition. This is exactly geometric integrality of $C_j\otimes_{A_j}\kappa(q)$. The same single $b$ works for all $j\geq b$ and all their primes, as required.

Step 3: count 1 is equivalent to geometric irreducibility, via 004W (a space is the union of its components) and lem-sbc-subset-geometric-irreducibility with A=|Z| and Ω=k_s; elementary is fair, and the empty fibre has count 0.
